interrex.title: The Classical Quarterly — The Five-Day Interregnum in the Roman Republic
interrex.context: Discusses patrician membership, restoration of auspices and successive interreges. Notes 60–61 and 68 quote Cicero and distinguish the first interrex from the one who presided at elections.

hortensia.title: Cambridge — Power and Process under the Republican Constitution
hortensia.context: Assemblies: The Plebs. Lex Hortensia (287 BCE) gives resolutions of the plebs the binding force of laws. Chapter also discusses Licinio-Sextian access to the consulship in the fourth century BCE.

agatho.title: Getty — Grave Relief of a Silversmith
agatho.context: Object 96.AA.40, first quarter of the first century CE. The inscribed P[UBLII] L[IBERTUS] names Publius's freedman, Publius Curtilius Agatho, a silversmith.

peculium.title: Cambridge — The Roman Law of Slavery, chapter VIII
peculium.context: The chapter distinguishes the master's legal title from a slave's administration of a separate fund, which could support business dealings.

dictator.title: Cambridge — The Consul at Rome, Appointment of a dictator
dictator.context: The summary distinguishes the Senate's decision and the consul's formal appointment in the ordinary procedure, with exceptional cases.

offices.title: Cambridge — The City of Rome: Scene of Politics and Growing Metropolis
offices.context: Title and Number table and paragraph following it: the magistracies, ten tribunes elected yearly, their sacrosanctity, and their ability to stop punishment by magistrates. Also reviews consular army commands, revision of Senate lists by censors, and praetors' commands in Sicily.

contracts.title: Polybius — Histories, Book VI §17
contracts.context: §17.2: censors let contracts for construction and repair of public buildings across Italy; §13.3: the Senate allocated funds for this work.

foreign.title: Cambridge — Access to Justice by Means of Arbitration in Roman Law
foreign.context: Chapter summary quotes Pomponius on establishing the praetor inter peregrinos, with jurisdiction mainly between non-citizens, when a single urban praetor was insufficient.

salii.title: Cambridge — Social Standing and Its Impact on Careers
salii.context: Section 2.3.1 identifies Salii as a patrician priesthood during the Principate.

patron.title: Gaius — Institutes, Book III §40
patron.context: §40 discusses the patron's inheritance when a freedman died intestate without a suus heres under the Twelve Tables.

tutors.title: The Met — Roman Art: A Resource for Educators
tutors.context: Roman family section identifies the education of the master's children as a role for some enslaved persons.
